transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I came in because I just cannot sit still when I’m supposed to. Like in the radiology suite, or even in class, it feels like I’m crawling out of my skin if I have to stay in one place too long. I’ll be trying to pay attention or just do what I’m supposed to do, but my whole body feels like it has to move.

I’ve tried to just tough it out for months, telling myself I should be able to handle it, but I still end up pacing, shifting around in my seat, standing up, or finding some excuse to move even when it’s probably not the right time. It’s gotten to the point where it feels like I need to talk to someone about it instead of just pretending it’s fine.
Did this restless feeling start after you began a medication or changed the dose of one?

Um… I don’t think so? Like, I’m trying to think through it carefully, because I know sometimes timing matters with that stuff, but I can’t point to a specific medication change where it suddenly started or got way worse right after.

I mean, I don’t really have a clear “oh, I started this pill and then the restless feeling began” kind of thing. It’s more like… this has just been there, and I’ve been dealing with it, and it’s gotten hard to ignore. But no, not that I’ve noticed with starting something new or changing a dose.
Since you were a child, have you often had trouble sitting still?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, that part goes way back. My parents still bring up stuff from elementary school, like parent-teacher conferences where the teacher would say I was constantly out of my seat, or I’d call out before I was supposed to, or I’d rush ahead before they even finished giving the directions.

And that was not, like, a recent thing from radiology training or college stress or something. It was happening way before middle school. I kind of grew up hearing, “You need to stay seated,” or “Wait until they finish explaining,” so… yeah, trouble sitting still has been there since I was a kid.
Have you ever had a period where your mood was unusually high or irritable?

Um… I’m not really sure how to answer that. Like, I’ve definitely had times where I’m irritated or kind of wound up, but I don’t know if I’d call it an “unusually high” mood or anything like that.

When you say “period,” do you mean like days where I’m noticeably different from normal, or just moments where I’m in a really good mood or snap at people? Because I can get frustrated, especially when I’m feeling stuck or like I can’t move around, but I don’t know that I’ve had some separate stretch where my mood was, like, abnormally elevated. I’m not saying impossible, I just… nothing obvious comes to mind the way you’re describing it.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks or conversations?

I’m not totally sure how to separate that from just being tired or bored, honestly. I mean, I do notice my mind can kind of drift if something is really repetitive or if someone is talking for a long time, but I don’t know if it’s more than what other people deal with.

In conversations, sometimes I’ll realize I’m thinking ahead about what I’m going to say, or I’m looking at something else in the room, and then I’m like, wait, I should probably be listening better. But I wouldn’t know how to rate whether that’s “often” or clinically a problem, if that makes sense.

For tasks, it depends a lot on what the task is. If it’s something interesting or hands-on, it’s easier. If it’s just sitting there reading or going through something slow, then yeah, my focus is not great. But I don’t know if I’d say I have a clear answer beyond that.
When you feel like you can’t sit still, is it usually because you’re feeling anxious or worried?

Not usually, no. I mean, I can be stressed sometimes, like anyone, but the “I can’t sit still” feeling doesn’t really feel like worry to me. It’s more physical, like I’m crawling out of my skin or there’s this pressure in me to get up and move.

That’s honestly a big reason I came in. In the radiology suite or in class, when I’m supposed to stay in one spot and just sit there or stand still and wait, I start shifting around, bouncing my leg, pacing if I can, or I’ll find some excuse to go do something even if it’s not really necessary. I’ve tried for months to just tough it out and tell myself to stay put, but it still happens. It’s not like I’m sitting there thinking, “Oh no, something bad is going to happen.” It’s more like my body just won’t let me be still.
Have you ever had a time when your energy was much higher than usual and you were doing a lot more than normal?

Yeah, but I don’t know if it’s like a “period” in the way you’re asking, like a sudden episode where I’m a totally different person. It’s more like… most days I just keep moving from one thing to the next.

Like I’ll go from class to clinicals, then to the gym, then I’ll run errands, and if there’s any empty space in the day, I almost automatically fill it with something. Even if I technically could go home and relax, I’ll think, okay, I should stop at the store, or clean my car, or go work out, or do something, because just sitting around feels almost impossible. It’s not really that I’m in some amazing mood or feeling unstoppable. It’s more like if I stop, I get really uncomfortable, so I keep adding stuff to my day.

So yes, my energy is high a lot, but it feels kind of constant rather than like one specific unusual stretch.
Have you ever had a distinct period when you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?

I don’t think so, not in a clear way. Like, I’ve definitely had nights where I didn’t sleep enough because of school or clinical stuff or just staying up too late, and then the next day I kind of push through because I have to. But I wouldn’t say I felt fully energized in a weird way, if that’s what you mean.

Usually if I get less sleep, I can feel it. I might still be moving around a lot, because that’s kind of how I am, but it doesn’t feel like I magically don’t need sleep. I’ll feel tired or foggy underneath it, even if I’m still restless. So no, I can’t really think of a distinct stretch where I only needed a few hours and felt great or unusually powered up.
Do you often have trouble getting organized and finishing tasks?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because it depends what you mean by organized. I don’t think of that as the main problem I’m here for, if that makes sense.

Like, I can get through things when there’s a clear structure or when I know exactly what has to happen, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m more disorganized than other people. And with finishing tasks… I mean, I finish things I have to finish, but I’d have to think about it more to know if it’s actually a pattern or just normal school/work stress.

So I guess my honest answer is: maybe sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d say “often” without thinking through examples.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things?

I mean… I worry about things, yeah, but I don’t know if I’d say I spend a lot of time worrying about all different kinds of things. It’s not like I’m constantly sitting there thinking something terrible is going to happen, at least not that I’ve really noticed.

I’ll stress about normal stuff, like school or whether I’m keeping up with what I’m supposed to do, but it feels more like regular pressure than me being stuck in worry all day. I guess I’d have to pay more attention to it, because I don’t usually think of myself as a super anxious person. If anything, I’m usually just trying to get through whatever’s in front of me.
Do you often put off or avoid tasks that require sustained mental effort, like reading, paperwork, or studying?

I’m not sure, honestly. Like, I know everybody puts off studying or paperwork sometimes, so I have a hard time knowing where the line is between “normal procrastination” and it being a bigger pattern.

With reading or studying, I guess it depends on what it is and how much pressure there is. If it’s something I know I absolutely have to get done, I usually find some way to do it, even if it’s not pretty or perfectly planned out. But I don’t know if I’d say I avoid it because it takes mental effort, exactly. Sometimes I just don’t start right away, and then later I’m like, “Okay, now I really have to do this.” But I haven’t really tracked whether that happens often enough to call it a real thing.

Paperwork is kind of the same. I don’t love it, but I don’t know many people who do. So… maybe sometimes I put it off, but I’m not sure I can confidently say I often avoid those kinds of tasks. I’d probably need to think through specific examples.
Does this need to move happen even when you're relaxed, like at home watching TV or hanging out?

Yeah, it does. That’s actually kind of the main reason I came in, because it’s not just when I’m stressed or in a situation where I’m supposed to be “on.” It’s like even if I’m technically relaxed, my body doesn’t get the memo.

Like at home, if I’m watching TV, I’m still shifting around a lot, changing positions, getting up for no real reason, walking to the kitchen, coming back, sitting down, then realizing I’m bouncing my leg or I need to stand again. And in the radiology suite or in class, it’s worse because I’m supposed to stay still and focused, and then I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I’ll try to tough it out, but after a while I end up pacing, shifting, or finding some excuse to move around.

It’s been going on for months, and I kept thinking I could just deal with it or force myself to sit still, but it hasn’t really worked. It’s not like I’m trying to be annoying or impatient. It just feels really uncomfortable to stay still for too long.
